title: Nuisance protects interests in the use and enjoyment of land and certain public rights

content.overview: Nuisance protects interests in the use and enjoyment of land and certain public rights. Private nuisance requires substantial and unreasonable interference; public nuisance concerns interference with a right common to the public.
content.glance: Nuisance protects interests in the use and enjoyment of land and certain public rights. Private nuisance requires substantial and unreasonable interference; public nuisance concerns interference with a right common to the public.
content.study: Nuisance protects interests in the use and enjoyment of land and certain public rights. Private nuisance requires substantial and unreasonable interference; public nuisance concerns interference with a right common to the public.\n\nSturges v Bridgman and Municipal Council, Ratlam show that nuisance is contextual. Locality, duration, intensity, foreseeability and reasonableness matter.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: Sturges v Bridgman and Municipal Council, Ratlam show that nuisance is contextual. Locality, duration, intensity, foreseeability and reasonableness matter.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: There is no single Indian Nuisance Act. Common-law doctrine is supplemented by municipal and environmental statutes. Statutory authority must be analysed carefully.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Protected private land interest or public right. 2. Substantial interference. 3. Unreasonable or otherwise actionable conduct. 4. Causation. 5. Special injury where required for a private public-nuisance action.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Evidence includes duration, frequency, intensity, measurements, expert reports, photographs and locality evidence.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Private nuisance is ordinarily litigated in civil court; public nuisance may also engage statutory remedies. Check limitation and special forums.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Doctrine Satisfied
examples.body: Nuisance turns on substantial and unreasonable interference; public authorities cannot evade statutory nuisance duties merely by pleading financial difficulty.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: The interference must satisfy the legal threshold of substantiality and unreasonableness or the applicable public-nuisance rule.
